newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan sees no need to restrict growth.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan sees no need to restrict growth.

text.p: The Brazilian economy is showing signs of picking up and the government does not plan to take measures to restrict growth, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said.
In an interview with newspaper Jornal do Brasil, Malan said it was "reasonable" to expect economic growth of between four and 4.5 percent in 1997.

Numbers from the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) showed growth of 2.4 percent in the 12 months to September 30 while growth in the third quarter would be around 3.6 percent and about 3.1 percent for 1996 as a whole, he said.
The IBGE also saw 7.2 percent growth in the third quarter of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995, Malan said.

"Whoever looks at these numbers will see we are clearly in a recovery phase," the minister told Jornal do Brasil. "There is no reason to talk about recession because we didn't have one, we don't have one and we won't have one.
"There is also no reason to talk about an excessive rate of growth that has to be immediately fought with restrictive measures," Malan continued.
